newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African rand was dizzied by see-saw action on Friday, with importer nerves and a sudden dearth of dollar supply wiping out most of the week's gains before the weekend.
The rand, having traded in a three-cent range over the Friday's session, posted an official close of 4.5635/5665 to the dollar from 4.5585/5615 Thursday.
"I'm surprised the exporers didn't come in at 4.5600. It might need the Reserve Bank on Monday if this continues," said one dealer.
Another dealer said many market players significantly long dollars had squared positions early but found they'd sold too much when importers started to itch for greenbacks.
"There were very few early corporate flows. Banks got short dollars and then found they had to keep buying them back once the offshore guys and the importers got in," he added.
In the options market three-month implied volatilities were left around 7.50, a far cry from a 30-day historical rate of close to 2.5.
Dealers said the volatilities suggested some short-term nerves but noted the afternoon's physical market action was unrelated.
"I wouldn't want to be long those vol's right now, and there are plenty that are. I'm not sure how long they can be justified up there if the rand hugs the (longer term) 4.53-58 range," said one.
Cross rate action saw the local unit last at 0.4027/4031 from 0.4025/4029 Thursday.
Against the yen, the rand was fetching 25.4932/5318 from a previous level of 25.4462/4849 and on sterling it was last at 7.5990/6085 from 7.6255/6351.
Benchmark gilts finally made it back below the figure at the close after an earlier attempt failed.
The bellwhether R150 long bond was last at 13.995 percent from Thursday's close of 14.04 percent.
The loan notched up its latest 17-month low of 13.965 in early morning dealings.
Dealers said the market was waiting for next week's economic data for direction with some players beginning to murmur hopes of an early interest rate cut should the figures come in as expected.
"The bond's done a hell of a lot this week. The guys are waiting for something fundamental to give it direction," said one dealer.
June trade, M3, private sector credit, CPI and reserves figures are due from Monday next week. The data are expected to back economists' call for easier monetary policy.
The South African Reserve Bank said the money market shortage fell to 6.885 billion rand on Thursday from 7.860 billion rand on Wednesday.
The shortage has narrowed by almost one billion rand for three days running.
On the money market, offered rates for three-month NCDs continued Thursday's move down, falling to 15.55 percent, while the 90-day BA rate lined up at 15.00 percent.
Foreigners bought 428.39 million rands worth of South African bonds on Thursday after buying 460.82 million on Wednesday, the Bond Exchange said.
Bond Exchange turnover leapt to 53.4 billion rand on Thursday -- a settlement day -- from 11 billion rand on Wednesday.
-- Justin McCamish, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
